title: convolvulus dorycnium subsp. oxysepalus
intro: Convolvulus dorycnium subsp. oxysepalus, commonly known as the annual bindweed, is a plant species within the morning glory family, Convolvulaceae. The annual bindweed has been traditionally used in folk medicine due to its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help in reducing pain, swelling, and promoting wound healing. The therapeutic actions of Convolvulus dorycnium subsp. oxysepalus include its potential to exhibit analgesic, antiseptic, and antispasmodic effects, making it a valuable resource in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
